+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+source = str(ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet")
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+metadata = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT MIN(crash_date) AS min_date,
+           MAX(crash_date) AS max_date,
+           COUNT(*) AS crash_rows,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_pedestrians_killed IS NULL) AS null_pedestrian_killed
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    """,
+    [source],
+).fetchdf()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::BIGINT AS pedestrian_deaths
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """,
+    [source],
+).fetchdf()
+
+# Keep all requested calendar years in the output, including any year with no rows.
+annual = (
+    annual.set_index("year")
+    .reindex(range(2013, 2026), fill_value=0)
+    .rename_axis("year")
+    .reset_index()
+)
+annual["pedestrian_deaths"] = annual["pedestrian_deaths"].fillna(0).astype("int64")
+annual.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+
+max_date = pd.to_datetime(metadata.loc[0, "max_date"])
+year_2025_complete = max_date >= pd.Timestamp("2025-12-31")
+
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+bars = ax.bar(annual["year"], annual["pedestrian_deaths"], color="#277DA1", width=0.72)
+ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%d", padding=3, fontsize=8)
+ax.set_title("Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes, 2013–2025")
+ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+ax.set_xticks(annual["year"])
+ax.set_ylim(0, max(annual["pedestrian_deaths"].max() * 1.12, 1))
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+if not year_2025_complete:
+    ax.text(
+        0.99,
+        0.98,
+        f"2025 data through {max_date:%b %-d}",
+        transform=ax.transAxes,
+        ha="right",
+        va="top",
+        fontsize=8,
+        color="#555555",
+    )
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+answer_note = (
+    f"2025 is partial through {max_date:%B %-d, %Y}. "
+    if not year_2025_complete
+    else ""
+)
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Total pedestrians killed in crashes, summed from number_of_pedestrians_killed",
+            "denominator": "None; annual count",
+            "grouping": "Crash year (2013–2025)",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "An annual total directly answers how many pedestrians were killed in each year.",
+            "probability": 1.0,
+            "answer": answer_note
+            + "Annual pedestrian deaths were "
+            + ", ".join(
+                f"{int(row.year)}: {int(row.pedestrian_deaths)}"
+                for row in annual.itertuples(index=False)
+            )
+            + ".",
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing directly answers the number of pedestrian deaths in each requested year, and the bars show the year-to-year totals. "
+                "Summing the crash-level pedestrian fatality counts is the appropriate measure of people killed, rather than counting crashes. "
+                "It does not show population-adjusted risk or explain why the totals changed."
+            ),
+        }
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print("Dataset metadata:")
+print(metadata.to_string(index=False))
+print("Annual pedestrian fatalities:")
+print(annual.to_string(index=False))
*** End Patch
